sampling_model.design: Fixed cohort-stratified repeated cross sections at a common baseline and dates \(1,\ldots,T\), with cohort \(g\) treated from date \(g\) onward.
sampling_model.units: Independent Gaussian cohort-time cell means with known variance \(\sigma^2/(Nq_g)\) at each wave.
sampling_model.treatment: For each \(t\le T-m\), cohort \(g\le t\) is compared with the pooled set \(C_t\); no untreated cohort remains for the target at \(T\).
sampling_model.overlap: Fixed shares satisfy \(c_q/T\le q_g\le C_q/T\), so \(q_{>t}>0\) at every score date used by the experiment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated inside the exact Gaussian score experiment. Calendar smoothness and centered bounded cohort deviations determine worst-case affine bias through the explicitly defined leverage functionals \(H(a)\) and \(D(a)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 3.3, Proposition 5, shows that sufficiently long-run nonnegative weighted effects are not identified without extrapolation when no never-treated units remain.
The paper identifies group-time ATTs, defines calendar aggregations, and provides simultaneous inference for identified collections.
Proposition 1 derives the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function and its efficiency bound for the two-period ATT.
Gaussian linear-functional difficulty is characterized through a modulus, and affine minimax rules are near global minimax rules.
Known-variance Gaussian confidence procedures over convex regression classes are characterized by ordered moduli and sharp expected-length bounds.
Theorem 3.1 on pp. 15--16 derives a simple honest interval and its Holder boundary bias--variance calibration for nonparametric regression.
Uniformly valid DiD confidence sets are constructed under bounded post-treatment deviations from observed pre-trends.
Loewner covariance dominance and Anderson's theorem order Gaussian procedures for symmetric convex acceptance regions.

body.tldr: Fixed cohort-stratified repeated cross sections induce an exact Gaussian not-yet-treated score experiment with a newly derived contemporaneous exhaustion term and a shared nested-baseline Gram term. The paper formulates the resulting baseline-cancellation Pareto program, proves pooled and baseline-cancelled feasible geometries, and gives an explicit equal-share certificate showing why small cohort-deviation leverage cannot be combined with the fast energy bound along a canonical growing-calendar sequence. Global minimax MSE and uniformly honest expected length are characterized, with explicit constants, by the exact nested covariance modulus. Converting that modulus into the candidate closed-form calendar functional remains open; the matched-date-block calculation applies only to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\).

project_justification.gap: Staggered-DiD work identifies effects only while valid comparisons remain, whereas Gaussian optimal-recovery work conditions on an already supplied operator and covariance. Neither literature derives the nested score covariance, separates contemporaneous exhaustion from shared-baseline cancellation, or studies the resulting coefficient Pareto frontier.
project_justification.niche: The paper treats late-calendar ATT inference as a growing, known-covariance Gaussian inverse problem. Its operator-specific content is the exact score covariance, the exposed affine coefficient program, two covariance geometries, and a rigorous obstruction to a tempting separable transport certificate.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the score law, defines a computable baseline-cancellation Pareto frontier, constructs pooled and baseline-cancelled affine channels, proves the fast-channel energy lower bound and a canonical baseline obstruction, and obtains exact-modulus minimax MSE and honest-length bounds. It leaves the matching intermediate Pareto lower bound, and therefore any closed calendar phase diagram, explicit as an open question.

body.related_work: Callaway and Sant'Anna provide the group-time causal effects and calendar aggregation underlying the target. Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess show why long-run event-study comparisons disappear, motivating extrapolation but not supplying its inference frontier. Sant'Anna and Zhao provide a two-period repeated-cross-section efficiency benchmark. Donoho's Gaussian modulus results and Armstrong and Kolesar's bias-aware interval theory supply generic optimal-recovery architecture once an operator and covariance are given; they do not derive the nested staggered-DiD score covariance or a bounded baseline-cancellation construction. Armstrong and Kolesar's direct-regression Holder calculations therefore do not establish the candidate nested calendar rate. Rambachan and Roth address sensitivity to untreated-trend violations rather than bounded heterogeneity of the treatment-effect surface. The matched-date-block calculation is a finite-sample calibration for \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\), not an ordering or rate transfer to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\).
body.technical_internal_limitation: The matching lower interpolation of the baseline-cancellation Pareto frontier is not proved. In particular, the available obstruction rules out one four-inequality fast certificate along \(m=1\), \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\), but it neither rules out every bounded lift nor proves that the exact nested modulus is incomparable to every closed-form rate. Equal within-date marginals also do not order \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\) and \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\). The exact Gaussian analysis does not cover nuisance estimation or non-Gaussian approximation error.
body.honest_scope: The proved headline consists of the exact nested score covariance, the explicit coefficient-energy and bias map, the two feasible covariance geometries, the canonical baseline-Gram obstruction, and global MSE and interval-length bounds in terms of \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\). The candidate diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\), its minimizing depth, and the matched-date-block Holder rate are not transferred to the nested experiment. The intermediate Pareto interpolation and smoothness adaptation remain open-ended questions.
body.interpretation: Two different uses of late score cells are now visible. Pooled one-date weights keep cohort-deviation bias small but retain shared-baseline noise; signed weights spread over separated reverse-date blocks can cancel that baseline term at the cost of constant cohort-deviation leverage. The exact nested modulus chooses over the full feasible geometry. The displayed candidate calendar functional records useful bias--variance scales, but it is not yet an identified closed form for that choice.
